properties.name: A finding another record had refuted still read as current, because the detector reads the edge and the age computation reads the date — two surfaces answering different questions about closure
properties.statement:
FOUND 2026-09-07, and the finding that produced it is a correction of the agent's own claim from twenty minutes earlier.

WHAT WAS OBSERVED. `fact:a-contract-is-the-one-thing-reflow2-cannot-attach-evidence-to` (2026-08-21) claimed VERIFIES could not target an Interface, so no contract in any design could carry a check. Interface was added to that target list on 2026-08-22, the day after. On 2026-08-31 a session drew an INVALIDATES edge onto the finding with a thorough note quoting its headline and showing it false, measured against all three published contracts. And on 2026-09-07 an agent ran search_design while brainstorming, met the finding with NO marker of any kind, read it as live, and re-derived the conclusion the design had already held for a week.

THE AGENT'S FIRST DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED HERE SO IT IS NOT REPEATED. It reported to Anthony that the finding had sat wrong for sixteen days and that the overtaken-defect detector had a gap because it filters on fact_type=defect. Measured afterwards: the detector reads INCOMING INVALIDATES and skips any fact that carries one, so it was CORRECTLY SILENT the whole time. There was no sixteen-day gap and no detector defect. Widening the fact_type filter, which is what the agent proposed and was asked to build, would have changed nothing about this case.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE, and it only appears once both sides are read together: CLOSURE IS ONE QUESTION WITH TWO AVAILABLE ANSWERS, and the two surfaces each read a different one. A claim can end because its own `valid_to` passed, or because a later record INVALIDATED it. `crates/reflow2-core/src/dates.rs::claim_age` computes `expired` from `valid_to` alone - it takes a property bag and structurally CANNOT see an edge - while the gap detector reads the edge and never looks at `valid_to` for this purpose. An invalidation sets no `valid_to`, so a refuted finding is closed for the detector and current for every read surface. Both pieces of code behaved exactly as written. Neither was wrong about its own question.

WHY THE READ SURFACE IS THE WORSE HALF TO GET WRONG: a detector reports to whoever runs it, at a boundary. `search_design` is what a person or an agent meets FIRST, in the middle of thinking about something else, and a record returned with no marker is read as true. The failure mode is not a missed alert; it is a confident wrong belief formed from the design's own memory.

THE FIX, at the cause rather than at the instance. `DesignGraph::claim_age_of` is one graph-aware computation that answers both halves, and both read surfaces - search_design and topic_report - go through it. `ClaimAge` gains `superseded_by`, kept DISTINCT from `expired` because a claim that ran out on its own terms is not a claim something refuted, and carrying the invalidating record's ID rather than a boolean because a reader told their source was overturned needs to be able to go and read what overturned it.

FAILING FIRST, OBSERVED: crates/reflow2-core/tests/a_superseded_finding_does_not_read_as_current.rs was written before the field existed and failed on its absence, then on three real assertions once the fixture was right. All three pass now. The test pins the CLASS - that both surfaces agree, and that the two kinds of closure stay distinguishable - not the one fact.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED. No sweep was run for other pairs of surfaces that compute the same question differently; this one was found by tripping over it. And nothing here decides whether an invalidation should ALSO set valid_to at write time - it is deliberately not done, because that would put the burden on every future invalidator to remember, which is the instruction-with-no-detector shape this project has measured failing more than once.
